name: Question 6
problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.3x-0.1y=0.6 \\ 0.6x+0.8y=0.2\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.3x-0.1y=0.6 & |\,\times 10 \\ 0.6x+0.8y=0.2 & |\,\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}3x-y=6 \\ 6x+8y=2\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we divide the second equation by $(-2),$ we will get a $-3x$ term in the second equation that can cancel with the $3x$ term in the first equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-y=6 &  \\ 6x+8y=2 & |\,÷(-2)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}3x-y=6 \\ -3x-4y=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{3x}-y & =6 \\ -\cancel{3x}-4y & =-1 \\ (-y-4y) & =(6-1) \\ -5y & =5 \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $y=-1$ into the equation $3x-y=6$ to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-y & =6 \\ 3x-(-1) & =6 \\ 3x & =5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=\frac{5}{3}$ and $y=-1.$

{0.3x−0.1y=0.60.6x+0.8y=0.2

a
x=53, y=−1
b
x=1, y=−3
c
x=73, y=1
d
x=43, y=−2
e
x=2, y=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by 10, as follows:

{0.3x−0.1y=0.6|×100.6x+0.8y=0.2|×10⟹{3x−y=66x+8y=2

Notice that if we divide the second equation by (−2), we will get a −3x term in the second equation that can cancel with the 3x term in the first equation:

{3x−y=66x+8y=2|÷(−2)⟹{3x−y=6−3x−4y=−1

Adding the two equations eliminates the x-variable and allows us to solve for y:

3x−y=6−3x−4y=−1(−y−4y)=(6−1)−5y=5y=−1

Finally, we can substitute y=−1 into the equation 3x−y=6 to solve for x:

3x−y=63x−(−1)=63x=5x=53

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is x=53 and y=−1.
